introduction: Hub gains an on-demand operation, POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/branches/:name/push and the matching `afc workspace push` command, that pushes one named branch from a workspace's trunk to the workspace's `origin` with the stored git credential. The push is serialized with other trunk operations, fast-forward only unless forced, refuses carry-patch-owned branches, never leaks the credential, and records every push attempt as a `hub.branch.push` audit event; the archive's existing push keeps its behaviour.

glossary.bound PAT: A personal access token bound to one workspace slug (spec 33); the binding guard answers 404 for any other slug.
glossary.error-type message prefix: The rule that messages for this route's own error types (branch_not_found, integration_branch, patch_branch, protected_branch, non_fast_forward, forge_*) begin with `<error_type>: `.
glossary.integration branch: On a carry_patch workspace, the workspace's integration_branch column, or `deploy` when that column is empty; hub builds it during rebuilds.
glossary.origin: The trunk's git remote pointing at the workspace's git_url on the forge.
glossary.push attempt: Any outcome after hub has handed the push to the go-git transport: success, up_to_date, non_fast_forward and every forge_* failure (including forge_unreachable and forge_timeout). Not attempts: refusals before the push, the secrets-store 500, and the 500 for a trunk that cannot be opened or has no origin.
glossary.registered patch branch: On a carry_patch workspace, a branch name that has a patches row whose status is not `deleted`.
glossary.scrub: The local text sanitizer of this route: replaces the credential's password or token with [redacted], removes URL userinfo, repeats until stable, and truncates to 1024 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary.
glossary.trunk: The workspace's main git clone on hub, at <workspace root>/<slug>/trunk, from which branches are pushed.
glossary.workspace lock: The per-slug lock from internal/wslock taken with TryLock; operations that cannot take it answer 409 workspace_busy.
glossary.workspace's own branch: The workspace's `branch` column, or, when that column is null, the branch the trunk's HEAD points to as read while the workspace lock is held.

requirements.title: The branch push route, its request and its answer
requirements.rationale: A caller needs a single, explicit route that gets a branch from hub's trunk onto the forge and tells it exactly what happened.

criteria.condition: an authorized caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/branches/:name/push for an existing branch of an active, ready workspace and the forge accepts the push
criteria.action: push refs/heads/<name> of the trunk to refs/heads/<name> on origin and answer with the branch, the local tip offered to origin, the remote and the remote URL
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {branch: string, sha: 40-hex string, remote: "origin", remote_url: string, result: "pushed"|"up_to_date"|"forced"}

criteria.action: for any branch name sent as a single path segment with '/' escaped as %2F, percent-decode the segment as sent exactly once, so that fix%2F42-nil-map names fix/42-nil-map and a%2525b names a%25b
criteria.contract: the decoded name is the value of `branch` in the 200 answer and the ref pushed

criteria.condition: the request path contains an unescaped '/' inside the branch name
criteria.action: match no route and send nothing to the forge
criteria.contract: the router's not-found answer (HTTP 404); no audit event is emitted

criteria.condition: the request has an empty body, or a JSON object body without `force`, or a JSON object body with unknown fields
criteria.action: treat `force` as false and ignore the unknown fields
criteria.contract: the push proceeds with the non-forced refspec

criteria.condition: the request body is not valid JSON, is not a JSON object, or carries a `force` value that is not a boolean
criteria.action: reject the request without taking the workspace lock or contacting the forge
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with apikit's error envelope; no audit event

criteria.action: set `result` to `up_to_date` when origin already had the offered commit on that branch and nothing was sent (even when force was given), to `forced` when force was given and the forge accepted an update, and to `pushed` for every other success; for any branch pushed successfully and unchanged since, a repeated call answers `up_to_date` and sends no objects
criteria.contract: the `result` field of the 200 answer

criteria.action: report `remote_url` as the workspace's git_url with URL userinfo removed when the URL has a scheme, and unchanged when it is an scp-style address (git@host:path)
criteria.contract: the `remote_url` field of the 200 answer contains no user:password@ segment for scheme URLs

criteria.action: begin every error message carrying one of the error types branch_not_found, integration_branch, patch_branch, protected_branch, non_fast_forward or forge_* with the error type followed by ": ", while the 404 `workspace not found`, the org-member 403 `forbidden`, the scope 403 and the 409 workspace_busy keep the messages shared with the other workspace routes
criteria.contract: apikit error envelope whose message starts with `<error_type>: ` for this route's own error types

requirements.title: Who may push
requirements.rationale: Pushing to the forge is a workspace write and must follow the same access rules and ordering as every other workspace write.

criteria.condition: the request carries no credential
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 401; no audit event; nothing sent to the forge

criteria.condition: the request uses a PAT bound to a different workspace than :slug, whatever its scopes
criteria.action: refuse the request before the scope check and before the workspace lookup
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with message `workspace not found`; no audit event

criteria.condition: the request uses a PAT that lacks the workspaces:write scope
criteria.action: refuse the request before the workspace is looked up
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with message `PAT requires workspaces:write scope to push branches` and no error_type; no audit event

criteria.condition: the slug is unknown, or the caller is not the owner, not an admin token and not a member of the workspace's org
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with message `workspace not found`; no audit event

criteria.condition: the caller is a member of the workspace's org but not its owner
criteria.action: refuse the request with the shared org-member write refusal
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type `forbidden` and message `org members have read-only access to this workspace`; no audit event

criteria.condition: the database fails while the workspace is looked up
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; no audit event

criteria.condition: the caller is the owner using an API key, the owner using a PAT with workspaces:write (including one bound to this slug), or an admin token
criteria.action: let the request proceed to the name, workspace and branch checks
criteria.contract: the answer is decided by 38-REQ-3 onward, not by an access refusal

requirements.title: Name and workspace preconditions
requirements.rationale: Requests that cannot name a branch of a usable trunk are refused before any trunk work starts.

criteria.condition: the decoded branch name breaks the rules of `git check-ref-format --branch` or starts with '-'
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock, naming the broken rule in the message
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type `branch_not_found` and a message such as `branch_not_found: "-x" is not a valid branch name: ref name must not start with '-'`; no audit event; the same answer whether or not the lock is held

criteria.condition: the workspace's status is not `active`
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with message `workspace is not active; push requires an active workspace`; no audit event

criteria.condition: the workspace's clone_status is not `ready`
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with message `workspace clone is not ready; clone_status must be 'ready' to push`; no audit event

requirements.title: Branches this route will not push
requirements.rationale: Carry-patch rules own the integration and patch branches, and the workspace's own branch must never be force-overwritten on the forge.

criteria.condition: the workspace mode is carry_patch and the name equals the integration branch (the integration_branch column, or `deploy` when it is empty)
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock, with a message saying hub builds this branch and it reaches the fork through REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type `integration_branch`; nothing sent to the forge; no audit event

criteria.condition: the workspace mode is carry_patch and the name has a patches row whose status is not `deleted`
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock, with a message pointing to PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type `patch_branch`; nothing sent to the forge; no audit event

criteria.condition: the workspace mode is carry_patch and the name is neither the integration branch nor a registered patch branch (including a name whose only patch row has status `deleted`)
criteria.action: push the branch as it would on a standard workspace
criteria.contract: the same answers as for a standard workspace

criteria.condition: `force` is true, the workspace's `branch` column is set, and the name equals it
criteria.action: refuse the request before taking the workspace lock, in either workspace mode
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type `protected_branch`; nothing sent to the forge; no audit event

criteria.condition: `force` is true, the workspace's `branch` column is null, and the name equals the branch the trunk's HEAD points to as read while the workspace lock is held
criteria.action: refuse the request after taking the lock and before the branch lookup, then release the lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type `protected_branch`; nothing sent to the forge; no audit event

criteria.condition: `force` is true, the `branch` column is null, and the trunk's HEAD cannot be read under the lock
criteria.action: refuse the request and release the lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; nothing sent to the forge; no audit event

criteria.condition: `force` is false and the name is the workspace's own branch
criteria.action: push the branch fast-forward only, like any other branch
criteria.contract: the answers of 38-REQ-1 and 38-REQ-6

criteria.condition: the database fails while the integration-branch, patch-branch or protected-branch decision is made
criteria.action: refuse the request without contacting the forge
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; no audit event

requirements.title: The lock, the branch lookup and the worktree
requirements.rationale: The push reads the trunk, so it must be serialized with every other trunk operation and must leave the worktree as the git server expects.

criteria.condition: another operation holds the workspace lock, including a rebuild in its fetch or final phase
criteria.action: refuse the request without waiting for the lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type `workspace_busy` and message `another operation is running on this workspace; retry later`; no audit event

criteria.condition: a rebuild is between its fetch phase and its final phase and does not hold the workspace lock
criteria.action: take the lock and proceed with the push without waiting for the rebuild
criteria.contract: the push answers per 38-REQ-6, not 409 workspace_busy

criteria.condition: refs/heads/<name> does not exist in the trunk when read under the lock
criteria.action: refuse the request and release the lock
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type `branch_not_found` and message `branch_not_found: branch "<name>" does not exist in the workspace`; no audit event

criteria.action: use as `sha` the commit refs/heads/<name> resolves to in the trunk, read while holding the lock just before the push
criteria.contract: the `sha` field of the 200 answer and of the audit event

criteria.action: hold the workspace lock until the push has ended, even if the caller has disconnected, and release it on every path including refusals, errors and panics-free failure returns
criteria.contract: after any answer (or after a disconnected push ends) a subsequent TryLock on the slug succeeds

criteria.condition: the commit the trunk's HEAD resolves to before the lock is released differs from the commit it resolved to when the lock was taken
criteria.action: hard-reset the trunk's worktree to the new HEAD commit before releasing the lock
criteria.contract: the trunk's worktree matches the new HEAD commit; the answer is unchanged

criteria.condition: the worktree hard reset fails, or HEAD has not moved, or HEAD cannot be read when the lock is taken or before it is released
criteria.action: leave the answer unchanged; on a failed reset log one warning, otherwise leave the worktree untouched
criteria.contract: the HTTP answer is the one the push produced

requirements.title: The push and the meaning of its outcome
requirements.rationale: Callers need each forge outcome mapped to the forge routes' established error vocabulary, and the forge's ref must never be left in an unknown state.

criteria.action: resolve the credential as the archive's push does (GIT_PAT, otherwise GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD, otherwise none) and push to the trunk's remote `origin` at the URL git_url with exactly the refspec refs/heads/<name>:refs/heads/<name>, or +refs/heads/<name>:refs/heads/<name> when `force` is true
criteria.contract: the forge receives only refs/heads/<name>, authenticated with the stored credential

criteria.condition: the secrets store fails while the credential is resolved
criteria.action: refuse the request without contacting the forge and log the failure without any secret
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with message `internal server error`; no audit event

criteria.condition: the push has not ended two minutes after it started, or the caller disconnects during the push
criteria.action: keep the push running despite the disconnect until it ends or the fixed two-minute deadline passes, and treat a passed deadline as a timeout
criteria.contract: on deadline: HTTP 504 with error_type `forge_timeout`; on disconnect: the outcome is logged and audited as if the caller were connected

criteria.condition: the push is not a fast-forward: go-git's client-side check refuses it, or the forge's per-ref status reports `non-fast-forward` or `fetch first`
criteria.action: list origin's refs once with the same URL, credential and deadline; name origin's commit in the message when the listing finds the branch and omit it when the listing fails; end with a force hint when the branch is not the workspace's own branch and with a hint to sync the workspace when it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type `non_fast_forward` and a message such as `non_fast_forward: origin's fix/42-nil-map is at <sha>, which is not in the workspace's branch; push with force to overwrite it`

criteria.condition: the forge answers 401 or reports authentication required, or answers 403 or reports authorization failed
criteria.action: refuse with a forge authentication error; for 401 the message says whether the workspace has no stored credential or the forge rejected it and names the credential kind (GIT_PAT or GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD), never its value
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with error_type `forge_unauthenticated` (401 case) or `forge_forbidden` (403 case)

criteria.condition: the forge reports the repository not found, or refuses the ref for a reason other than non-fast-forward (protected branch, hook declined)
criteria.action: refuse with the matching forge error, carrying the forge's scrubbed reason for a refused ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type `forge_not_found`, or HTTP 422 with error_type `forge_rejected`

criteria.condition: the push fails with a DNS, TCP or TLS failure, or with any other push failure not covered by the other outcomes
criteria.action: refuse with the matching forge error
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with error_type `forge_unreachable` (DNS/TCP/TLS) or `forge_error` (any other failure)

criteria.condition: the trunk cannot be opened, or `origin` is not configured in it
criteria.action: refuse the request as an internal failure that is not a push attempt
criteria.contract: HTTP 500; no audit event; no push-attempt warning log

requirements.title: Keeping the credential out
requirements.rationale: The stored git credential and any userinfo in git_url are secrets and must never leave hub through answers, events or logs.

criteria.action: for any input text and any credential secret, replace each occurrence of the secret with [redacted], remove URL userinfo, repeat both steps until the text stops changing, and cut the result to at most 1024 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary
criteria.contract: the output contains neither the secret nor any scheme://userinfo@ segment, is valid UTF-8, is at most 1024 bytes, and scrubbing it again leaves it unchanged

criteria.action: pass every error message this route returns or logs and every value of its audit event through the scrub, and never include the credential, the userinfo of git_url or go-git's full error chain in a response
criteria.contract: no response body, audit event or log line of this route contains the credential's secret or the userinfo of git_url

criteria.condition: a push attempt fails
criteria.action: log the failure exactly once at warning level with the fields workspace, branch, error_type and the scrubbed error, and log nothing under this rule for a successful push attempt
criteria.contract: exactly one warning log record per failed push attempt

criteria.condition: the route answers HTTP 500
criteria.action: log the internal error the way hub logs its internal errors, scrubbed
criteria.contract: the log line contains no credential secret or URL userinfo

requirements.title: The hub.branch.push audit event
requirements.rationale: Every attempt to change the forge, including a refused force-push, must leave a true record.

criteria.action: define the hub event type constant `hub.branch.push` next to the other hub event types, with a doc comment in their style
criteria.contract: the constant's value is the string `hub.branch.push`

criteria.condition: a push attempt ends with 200 pushed/forced/up_to_date, 409 non_fast_forward, 404 forge_not_found, 422 forge_rejected, 502 forge_unauthenticated/forge_forbidden/forge_unreachable/forge_error or 504 forge_timeout
criteria.action: emit exactly one hub.branch.push event with ResourceType "branch", ResourceID the branch name, Action "push", Workspace the slug and the actor from the credential
criteria.contract: exactly one hub.branch.push event per push attempt, visible to the audit emitter and on the SSE stream

criteria.action: fill the event metadata with branch, sha, force (bool), ok (bool), remote ("origin") and remote_url (userinfo removed), plus result when ok is true and error_type when ok is false, and never a credential or the forge's message text
criteria.contract: event metadata keys: branch, sha, force, ok, remote, remote_url, and exactly one of result / error_type

criteria.condition: the route answers 401, 403, 404 workspace not found, 404 branch_not_found, 400, 409 workspace_busy or any 500 (including a secrets-store failure and a trunk that cannot be opened or has no origin)
criteria.action: emit no hub.branch.push event
criteria.contract: zero hub.branch.push events for the request

criteria.condition: the caller disconnects before the push attempt ends
criteria.action: emit the event on the request context with its cancellation removed, recording the real outcome of the push
criteria.contract: exactly one hub.branch.push event whose ok/result/error_type match the push outcome

requirements.title: afc workspace push
requirements.rationale: Agents and operators need a CLI front end that reports the outcome, including the error type, through apikit's conventions.

criteria.condition: a user runs `afc workspace push <slug> <branch> [--force]`
criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/branches/<branch>/push with each path segment escaped (a '/' in the branch sent as %2F) and the body {"force": <bool>}
criteria.contract: the hub receives the escaped path and a JSON body whose force equals the presence of --force

criteria.condition: --force is given
criteria.action: write one warning line to stderr, before sending the request, saying that origin's branch may be overwritten
criteria.contract: exactly one warning line on stderr

criteria.condition: hub answers 200
criteria.action: print the response as one JSON document on stdout
criteria.contract: exit code 0

criteria.condition: hub answers with an error
criteria.action: print apikit's error envelope with hub's code and message
criteria.contract: exit code 1; for a non-fast-forward the output contains `non_fast_forward`

criteria.condition: the request fails on the client side (for example the hub cannot be reached or the client is misconfigured)
criteria.action: report the client error
criteria.contract: exit code 2

criteria.condition: the command is given fewer or more than two positional arguments
criteria.action: fail without contacting hub
criteria.contract: exit code 2; no HTTP request is sent

requirements.title: Shared push implementation and unchanged archive push
requirements.rationale: Reusing the archive's push for one branch must not change what archive and reclone do.

criteria.action: implement the archive's push to origin and the branch push with one shared push implementation
criteria.contract: both operations push through the same go-git push code path

criteria.condition: a workspace is archived or recloned
criteria.action: push refs/heads/*:refs/heads/* to origin at git_url with the resolved credential and no deadline, mapping go-git's already-up-to-date result to ErrAlreadyUpToDate, exactly as before this spec
criteria.contract: the archive push function keeps its three-argument signature (repoPath, gitURL, auth) and the existing archive and reclone tests pass without changes

execution_paths.title: The owner pushes a new branch to the forge through the API

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/branches/fix%2F42-nil-map/push with an API key and no body
authorizes the owner, decodes the name to fix/42-nil-map, checks the workspace is active and ready, and takes the workspace lock
resolves refs/heads/fix/42-nil-map in the trunk and the stored GIT_PAT credential
pushes refs/heads/fix/42-nil-map:refs/heads/fix/42-nil-map to origin within the two-minute deadline and releases the lock
creates refs/heads/fix/42-nil-map at the pushed commit
emits one hub.branch.push event with ok=true and result=pushed and answers 200 with remote_url stripped of userinfo

execution_paths.title: An agent pushes a branch with afc and repeats the call

steps.action: pushes the branch to origin and answers 200 with result pushed
prints the response as one JSON document and exits 0
finds origin already at the commit, sends no objects, emits a hub.branch.push event with result up_to_date and answers 200 up_to_date

execution_paths.title: A diverged branch is refused, then force-pushed

steps.action: runs `afc workspace push <slug> feature` while origin's feature has a commit the trunk lacks
pushes fast-forward only, gets a non-fast-forward refusal, lists origin's refs once and emits a hub.branch.push event with ok=false and error_type non_fast_forward
prints the error envelope whose message starts with `non_fast_forward:` and names origin's commit with a force hint, and exits 1
writes a warning line to stderr and sends body {"force": true}
checks feature is not the workspace's own branch, pushes +refs/heads/feature:refs/heads/feature and emits a hub.branch.push event with result forced
overwrites refs/heads/feature with the trunk's commit
